To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

antibiotic resistance in lactic bacteria and micrococci/staphylococci isolated from artisanal raw cow milk cheeses is frequent, and that antibiotic resistance does not necessarily exclude technological traits of interest for the food industry.
antibiotic resistance in lactic bacteria is common and that the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in artisanal cheeses could be a problem for cheese-making processes.
lactic acid bacteria from artisanal raw cow’s milk cheeses showed high rates of resistance to beta-lactams and streptomycin, whereas resistance to other antimicrobial agents was lower.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of antibiotic resistance profiles in the predominant lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and Microccocaceae/Staphyloccaceae of artisanal raw cheeses and the possible implications of these profiles for cheese making.
the identification and selection of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and Micrococcacea/Staphylococcae (MS) isolates that are potentially useful for use in the food industry.

a better knowledge of the potential risks associated with the presence of antibiotic-resistant microorganisms in cheeses, and it provides information on the potential implications of antibiotic resistance on cheese making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antibiotic-resistant strains are present in the microflora of artisanal cheeses, although the majority of them are not of technological interest.
the use of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in cheese making would depend on the particular case and the specific properties that the isolate would bring to the cheese.
the majority of isolates with the most desirable traits for food applications were also those that were the most sensitive to antimicrobial agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of isolates showed resistance to at least 1 of the antibiotics tested and that the most frequent resistances were those for which the highest rates of resistance are found in the environment.
the use of raw milk in the production of cheeses is a risk factor for the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in cheeses.
the majority of isolates from artisan cheeses were resistant to aminoglucosides, but the presence of isolates with technological interest was not associated with antibiotic resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotic resistance is a widespread phenomenon among the microflora of raw milk artisanal cheeses and that the most resistant species are the predominant species in the cheeses.
antibiotic resistance is a common trait among the predominant microbiota of artisanal raw milk cheesemaking, and it may affect cheese-making processes.
the presence of microorganisms with potential technological traits does not necessarily imply that they will be present in high numbers.
